verify.pass_when_text: Every active instance (pending, running, stopping or stopped) has MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=required. optional, or a missing value, fails.

vanta.test: EC2 instances use only IMDSv2 for the metadata service

steps: Check first (read-only, first block) that nothing still uses IMDSv1 on instance {resource_id}: the MetadataNoToken metric must be 0 and note the current hop limit.
Decide the hop limit: if containers on bridge networking run on the instance, they also need --http-put-response-hop-limit 2 (third block), otherwise they lose access to the metadata service.
Require IMDSv2 on instance {resource_id} by running the second block in its region.
Verify with describe-instances that HttpTokens is required and that the application keeps working.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# read-only: current hop limit and the MetadataNoToken metric of the last 14 days (a Sum greater than 0 means that something still uses IMDSv1)
aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "{resource_id}" --region "$REGION" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].MetadataOptions'
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name MetadataNoToken --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value="{resource_id}" --start-time "$(date -u -d '14 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --end-time "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --period 86400 --statistics Sum --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id "{resource_id}" --http-tokens required --http-endpoint enabled --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# only if containers on bridge networking run on the instance: allows the extra network hop to the metadata service
aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id "{resource_id}" --http-put-response-hop-limit 2 --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Decision before applying: confirm with the first block that nothing uses IMDSv1 and whether the instance runs containers (hop limit 2). No downtime and reversible with --http-tokens optional. Risk: an application or an old SDK that still uses IMDSv1 stops getting credentials. Before applying it, check the instance's CloudWatch MetadataNoToken metric (namespace AWS/EC2): if it is greater than 0, something is still using IMDSv1. Containers running on the instance need --http-put-response-hop-limit 2. If the instance belongs to an Auto Scaling group, the change is lost when the group replaces it: fix the launch template (CMP-002).

checks.title: Auto Scaling group launch templates require IMDSv2

verify.pass_when_text: The launch template version each group uses ($Latest, $Default or a numbered version) has MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=required. A group with a launch configuration (deprecated), a nonexistent template or a version without MetadataOptions fails.

vanta.test: IMDSv1 is disabled on EC2 Instances (ASG variant)

steps: Create a new version of the launch template of group {resource_id} with MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=required, starting from the latest version, and set it as the default version.
If the group uses a numbered version, point it to $Default so that it picks up the new version.
Start an instance refresh so that the existing instances are replaced with the new version, in an agreed window.
Verify that the refresh finishes successfully and that the new instances require IMDSv2 (CMP-001).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
ASG_NAME="{resource_id}"
LT_ID=$(aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names "$ASG_NAME" --region "$REGION" --query 'AutoScalingGroups[0].LaunchTemplate.LaunchTemplateId' --output text) && NEW_VERSION=$(aws ec2 create-launch-template-version --launch-template-id "$LT_ID" --source-version '$Latest' --launch-template-data '{"MetadataOptions":{"HttpTokens":"required","HttpEndpoint":"enabled"}}' --region "$REGION" --query 'LaunchTemplateVersion.VersionNumber' --output text) && aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id "$LT_ID" --default-version "$NEW_VERSION" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
ASG_NAME="{resource_id}"
LT_ID=$(aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names "$ASG_NAME" --region "$REGION" --query 'AutoScalingGroups[0].LaunchTemplate.LaunchTemplateId' --output text)
# the instance refresh only runs if the default version already requires IMDSv2
[ "$(aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-id "$LT_ID" --versions '$Default' --region "$REGION" --query 'LaunchTemplateVersions[0].LaunchTemplateData.MetadataOptions.HttpTokens' --output text)" = "required" ] && aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name "$ASG_NAME" --launch-template "LaunchTemplateId=$LT_ID,Version=\$Default" --region "$REGION" && aws autoscaling start-instance-refresh --auto-scaling-group-name "$ASG_NAME" --preferences '{"MinHealthyPercentage":90,"InstanceWarmup":300}' --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: The instance refresh replaces the group's instances one batch at a time (MinHealthyPercentage 90): a single-instance group has downtime, and anything that lives only on the instances' local disk is lost. Do it in an agreed window. Before applying, check the instances' MetadataNoToken metric: if an application uses IMDSv1, it breaks with the replacement. The commands assume a group with a direct LaunchTemplate; if it uses MixedInstancesPolicy, the template ID query is MixedInstancesPolicy.LaunchTemplate.LaunchTemplateSpecification.LaunchTemplateId. A group that still uses a launch configuration must be migrated to a launch template first. Quota: only one active instance refresh per group. The first block changes the launch template's default version for ALL of its users (other Auto Scaling groups, fleets, launches with $Default), not just this group: check with describe-launch-template-versions who uses it before applying.

checks.title: EC2 instances have an instance profile (IAM role) attached

verify.pass_when_text: Every active instance has an IamInstanceProfile. Without an instance profile, the application's credentials have to live on the instance (access keys), which is what the test aims to avoid.

vanta.test: Instances use IAM instance roles for AWS resource access

steps: Decide which permissions instance {resource_id} needs (the minimum; if only Systems Manager management is required, the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy).
If a suitable instance profile does not exist yet, create the EC2 role and the instance profile and associate them (first block), and attach the chosen policies.
Associate the instance profile with the instance (second block).
Verify with describe-instances that IamInstanceProfile is now listed.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
ROLE_NAME="__FILL_IN_ROLE_NAME__"
PROFILE_NAME="$ROLE_NAME"
# only if an instance profile with a role does not exist yet
aws iam create-role --role-name "$ROLE_NAME" --assume-role-policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}' && aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name "$PROFILE_NAME" && aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name "$PROFILE_NAME" --role-name "$ROLE_NAME"
remediation.notes: No downtime: the association is applied live. A newly created role has no permissions: least-privilege policies (a team decision) must be attached to it or it grants nothing. Right after creating the instance profile, the association may fail with InvalidParameterValue because of IAM propagation: retry after a few seconds. If the instance already uses access keys stored on disk, migrate them to the role and rotate them.

checks.title: Regions with EC2 instances have a load balancer spanning 2 or more Availability Zones

verify.pass_when_text: Each region with EC2 instances has at least one load balancer (application, network or classic) that spans 2 or more Availability Zones. It is a per-region test, like Drata's 130: if it fails, every instance in that region is reported. With no EC2 instances there is nothing to evaluate.

steps: Choose two public subnets (or private ones, if the load balancer is internal) in different Availability Zones of region {region}.
Create an Application Load Balancer in those subnets, a target group, and register instance {resource_id}.
Create the HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate and test the service through the load balancer.
Switch DNS to point at the load balancer and, to get real high availability, place instances in both zones (ideally in an Auto Scaling group, see CMP-005).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
LB_NAME="__FILL_IN_ALB_NAME__"
SUBNET_A="__FILL_IN_SUBNET_AZ_A__"
SUBNET_B="__FILL_IN_SUBNET_AZ_B__"
SG_ID="__FILL_IN_SECURITY_GROUP_ID__"
VPC_ID="__FILL_IN_VPC_ID__"
CERT_ARN="__FILL_IN_ACM_CERTIFICATE_ARN__"
SCHEME="__FILL_IN_ALB_SCHEME__"
TARGET_PORT="__FILL_IN_TARGET_PORT__"
# SCHEME (allowed values: internet-facing or internal) decides whether the service is exposed to the internet (internet-facing needs public subnets; internal needs none); TARGET_PORT is the port the instances listen on (target group protocol HTTP)
LB_ARN=$(aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name "$LB_NAME" --type application --scheme "$SCHEME" --subnets "$SUBNET_A" "$SUBNET_B" --security-groups "$SG_ID" --region "$REGION" --query 'LoadBalancers[0].LoadBalancerArn' --output text) && TG_ARN=$(aws elbv2 create-target-group --name "$LB_NAME-tg" --protocol HTTP --port "$TARGET_PORT" --vpc-id "$VPC_ID" --region "$REGION" --query 'TargetGroups[0].TargetGroupArn' --output text) && aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn "$TG_ARN" --targets "Id={resource_id}" --region "$REGION" && aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn "$LB_ARN" --protocol HTTPS --port 443 --certificates "CertificateArn=$CERT_ARN" --default-actions "Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=$TG_ARN" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: This is an architecture change, not a patch: plan it. Decide the scheme (__FILL_IN_ALB_SCHEME__ takes exactly internet-facing or internal; internet-facing exposes the load balancer to the internet, internal does not) and the instances' port: the command has no default for either. Cost: the ALB charges per hour plus per LCU consumed. A load balancer in 2 zones with a single instance behind it does not provide real high availability; capacity is needed in both zones. The load balancer's security group must allow traffic to the instances' security group. A single load balancer resolves the finding for all instances in the region. If the application only speaks HTTP, use an HTTP:80 listener and review the HTTPS redirect check.

checks.title: Regions with EC2 instances have at least one Auto Scaling group

verify.pass_when_text: Each region with EC2 instances has at least one Auto Scaling group. It is a per-region test, like Drata's 131: if it fails, every instance in that region is reported. With no EC2 instances there is nothing to evaluate.

steps: Create an AMI of instance {resource_id} without rebooting it.
Create a launch template with that AMI, the instance type, the instance's security group(s) and instance profile (placeholders SG_ID and INSTANCE_PROFILE) and IMDSv2 required.
Create an Auto Scaling group with that launch template in subnets of at least 2 Availability Zones, choosing its minimum, maximum and desired size (the group starts launching instances right away).
Shift traffic to the group and, once validated, retire the original instance.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
INSTANCE_ID="{resource_id}"
SUBNETS="__FILL_IN_SUBNETS_AZ_A_AND_AZ_B__"
ASG_NAME="__FILL_IN_ASG_NAME__"
INSTANCE_TYPE="__FILL_IN_INSTANCE_TYPE__"
SG_ID="__FILL_IN_SECURITY_GROUP_ID__"
INSTANCE_PROFILE="__FILL_IN_INSTANCE_PROFILE_NAME_OR_EMPTY__"
MIN_SIZE="__FILL_IN_MIN_SIZE__"
MAX_SIZE="__FILL_IN_MAX_SIZE__"
DESIRED_SIZE="__FILL_IN_DESIRED_SIZE__"
# SG_ID and INSTANCE_PROFILE are those of the original instance (set INSTANCE_PROFILE="" if it has none); the group launches a NEW instance with them, in the subnets of SUBNETS
PROFILE_JSON=""; [ -n "$INSTANCE_PROFILE" ] && PROFILE_JSON=",\"IamInstanceProfile\":{\"Name\":\"$INSTANCE_PROFILE\"}"
AMI_ID=$(aws ec2 create-image --instance-id "$INSTANCE_ID" --name "$ASG_NAME-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)" --no-reboot --region "$REGION" --query 'ImageId' --output text) && aws ec2 wait image-available --image-ids "$AMI_ID" --region "$REGION" && aws ec2 create-launch-template --launch-template-name "$ASG_NAME" --launch-template-data "{\"ImageId\":\"$AMI_ID\",\"InstanceType\":\"$INSTANCE_TYPE\",\"SecurityGroupIds\":[\"$SG_ID\"],\"MetadataOptions\":{\"HttpTokens\":\"required\"}$PROFILE_JSON}" --region "$REGION" && aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name "$ASG_NAME" --launch-template "LaunchTemplateName=$ASG_NAME,Version=\$Latest" --min-size "$MIN_SIZE" --max-size "$MAX_SIZE" --desired-capacity "$DESIRED_SIZE" --vpc-zone-identifier "$SUBNETS" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: This is an architecture change: the group launches a NEW instance, so the service is duplicated until the original is retired, and the data the instance keeps on local disk or on its own volume does not travel to the group (not suitable for stateful servers). create-image with --no-reboot does not guarantee file system consistency. Cost: AMI snapshots plus the new instance. The security group, the instance profile and the instance type must match the original instance (placeholders SG_ID, INSTANCE_PROFILE and INSTANCE_TYPE): without them the new instance would come up in the default security group with no IAM role. The desired size (DESIRED_SIZE) launches that many NEW instances immediately. A single group in the region resolves the finding for all of its instances.

checks.title: EC2 instances are managed by Systems Manager and have a patch association

verify.pass_when_text: Each instance is registered in Systems Manager with the agent online (PingStatus=Online) and has a Patch Manager patch state (describe-instance-patch-states). Instances that are not in the running state (for example stopped ones) cannot run the agent and are not evaluated.

steps: Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the role of instance {resource_id} (if it has no instance profile, see CMP-003).
Verify that the SSM agent is installed and that the instance reaches the service (internet egress or the ssm, ssmmessages and ec2messages VPC endpoints).
Create a State Manager association that runs AWS-RunPatchBaseline in Scan mode on a weekly schedule.
Wait for the first run and verify the patch state with describe-instance-patch-states.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
ROLE_NAME="__FILL_IN_ROLE_NAME__"
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name "$ROLE_NAME" --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
INSTANCE_ID="{resource_id}"
aws ssm create-association --name "AWS-RunPatchBaseline" --targets "Key=InstanceIds,Values=$INSTANCE_ID" --parameters 'Operation=Scan' --schedule-expression "cron(0 3 ? * SUN *)" --association-name "patch-scan-$INSTANCE_ID" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Scan only inventories the missing patches; it installs nothing and does not change the instance's software. Installing them (Operation=Install) is a separate decision, with a maintenance window, because it can reboot the instance. The instance role is a team decision; AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore is the minimum SSM policy. Without internet egress or VPC endpoints the agent does not register. On an instance whose agent has just registered, the patch state takes until the first run to appear. The agent comes preinstalled on recent Amazon Linux and Windows AMIs.
